offerText: Your first article is on me.

signal.text: Consumer Reports Wearable Privacy Audit dropped this morning. Beacon isn't rated; Apollo Neuro was scored C+ on retention policy. First-mover framing on trust is open for one publish cycle.

cards.title: Bedside manner: wearables' positioning problem
cards.angle: Consumer neurotech keeps marketing to biohackers when the real ROI is helping doctors run harder conversations. Reposition around that reader and the enterprise pipeline gets warmer.
cards.evidence: Beacon's investor teardown on The Information (July 2026) lists three enterprise sleep-clinic pilots. beaconlabs.com still opens with 'biohack your brain.'

cards.title: 12-hour sensors: the clinician trust threshold
cards.angle: Short datasets make clinicians skeptical. Battery life is not a spec issue, it is a credibility issue.
cards.evidence: Nature Sleep Medicine review (June 2026, doi:10.1038/nsm.2026.4471) cites 10-plus hours of continuous recording as the accepted clinical trust cutoff.

cards.title: Compliance moats wearable startups keep ignoring
cards.angle: FDA clearance is table stakes. The real moat is HIPAA-BAA-signed cloud storage, and it is cheaper to prove than most founders realize.
cards.evidence: Beacon's AWS re:Invent 2026 healthcare track talk (recording on YouTube) walks through a BAA-signed setup. The marketing site never surfaces it.

sources.title: AWS re:Invent 2026 healthcare track — Beacon Labs session

cards.title: Refresh the Mayo case study
cards.angle: The published Mayo case answers what you did, not what changed for the buyer. Three added questions surface the outcome numbers and turn it into a linkable asset.
cards.evidence: Public case study at beaconlabs.com/case/mayo (published June 2026) contains zero specific outcome numbers.

cards.title: Wearables' hidden B2B2C business model
cards.angle: The reviews complain about your app UX, but the real customer is the clinic that recommends you. Their UX starts with a clinician dashboard that does not exist yet.
cards.evidence: Amazon reviews for Beacon Ring average 4.1 stars from verified consumers and 4.8 stars from reviewers whose profiles identify as sleep clinicians.

cards.title: Wearable privacy: 2026's open trust category
cards.angle: The privacy-first wearable brand is unclaimed. Whoever writes the plain-language biometric-data manifesto owns the trust conversation for a decade.
cards.evidence: Consumer Reports 2026 Wearable Privacy Audit (September) shows every top-10 policy buries data-retention terms behind an appendix link.

cards.title: Pricing pages that negotiate against you
cards.angle: Anchor pricing at the enterprise tier and let self-serve buyers scroll past it. Right now your cheapest tier loads first and trains buyers to see a $29 product.
cards.evidence: beaconlabs.com/pricing loads $29/mo first. The Series A deck filed on Crunchbase (May 2026) references enterprise ACVs of $2,400 per seat per year.

cards.title: Peer review's silent marketing gap
cards.angle: Peer review is the highest-cost credibility you have, and it is not doing marketing work. Three studies exist and none of them appear on a conversion page.
cards.evidence: npj Digital Medicine paper (March 2026, doi:10.1038/npj.dm.2026.0142) is not linked from beaconlabs.com/product, /pricing, or /case pages.

cards.title: Developer wearables: the untold segment
cards.angle: Every API discussion is written for consumer app builders. The quiet users are contract research orgs, a whole category with its own vocabulary and its own buying signal.
cards.evidence: Beacon's public GitHub org shows three CRO-adjacent forks of beacon-sdk in Q3 2026. That signal never lands on the marketing site.

cards.title: Founder reading lists as authority
cards.angle: Your public reading list is more interesting than most of what you post. Publish it every two weeks with a one-line 'why this matters' for the sector.
cards.evidence: Three papers you cited on LinkedIn without framing in September 2026 (posts dated Sep 4, Sep 15, Sep 22) each pulled roughly 3x the engagement of your product posts.
